what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) lets a server do computations on data that remains encrypted the whole time, so the server never sees the raw data — but today's FHE is absurdly slow because each encrypted number balloons to thousands of times its original size, demanding enormous amounts of memory bandwidth. EFFACT is a combined software compiler and hardware chip design (targeting both FPGA, a reprogrammable chip, and ASIC, a fixed custom chip) that attacks this problem from every angle at once. A 'streaming' memory scheme keeps a small but fast on-chip memory (SRAM, essentially the chip's scratchpad) busy by fetching the next chunk of data from the large slow off-chip memory while the current chunk is still being processed, so the chip rarely sits idle waiting for data. Circuit-level tricks reuse the same arithmetic hardware units for multiple operations, cutting chip area without sacrificing speed. A shared instruction language lets the compiler target multiple FHE mathematical schemes (CKKS, BGV, BFV — different ways of structuring the encryption math) from a single codebase.
